newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money opens steady, seen unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money opens steady, seen unchanged.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 5.0-5.25 percent range in early Wednesday trade, little changed from Tuesday's close of 5.0-5.5 precent, dealers said.
They said call money rates were likely to remain at current levels or drop slightly as there was not much demand for funds ahead of the reporting day on Friday.
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.
The money market is largely inactive on Thursday as banks in India's capital centre of Bombay and several other centres are closed for a local holiday.
Dealers said the announcement of a 30 billion rupee three-year federal government bond auction for May 28 had not had much impact on rates.
They said rates could move up after the reporting day.

"Most banks have covered their positions ahead of the reporting Friday," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Rates will move up on Saturday or Monday as market players discount the outflows towards the three-year bond subscription."
